- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), as models tend to underreact to bearish signals.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30) — models often overreact to bullish sentiment, leading to lagged or delayed price spikes.
- Avoid sharp downward forecasts after recent spikes — models frequently overshoot downward momentum, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Lagged response to sentiment: if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, model should adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per day, not wait for 7–10 days.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true outcome by > 5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to underestimating late-period spikes — especially if sentiment is positive and rising. Add 1–2% buffer for final 5–7 days.
